reference: The runner has no `cal` executable in its /usr/bin:/bin reference PATH (confirmed by the initial parity submission). These honest contract checks use fixed facts from Python's independent Gregorian calendar arithmetic and Julian weekday arithmetic, applying the output shape and feature contracts documented in loadables/cal.c. No expected value is taken from candidate output; the test scripts emit a marker only after checking the stated calendar facts.
coverage: Gregorian month grid, weekday columns, and leap-day placement
Julian day-of-year values in a leap year
Three-column full-year layout with all month groups
Three-month and explicit before/after spans crossing a year boundary
Invalid month range and Bash usage status
Bash builtin type and help metadata
exclusions: No runnable GNU or util-linux cal oracle is installed in the validation environment, so calendar cases are contracts rather than claimed GNU parity.
Current-month output depends on the wall clock and is omitted from deterministic checks.
Exact -w week-number layout and options outside the documented subset remain uncovered.

cases.purpose: Check the documented 22-character Sunday-first month grid and independently known February 2024 weekday and leap-day cells.
cases.script:
out=$(cal 2 2024)
mapfile -t lines <<< "$out"
[[ ${lines[1]:0:20} == 'Su Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa' ]]
[[ ${lines[2]:12:2} == ' 1' ]]
[[ ${lines[6]:12:2} == '29' ]]
printf 'February 2024 leap grid verified\n'

cases.purpose: Check Monday-first headings and place September 1, 2024, a Sunday, in the final weekday column.
cases.script:
out=$(cal -m 9 2024)
mapfile -t lines <<< "$out"
[[ ${lines[1]:0:20} == 'Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su' ]]
[[ ${lines[2]:18:2} == ' 1' ]]
printf 'Monday-first grid verified\n'

cases.purpose: Check Julian day-of-year numbering independently: February 1, 2024 is day 32 and February 29 is day 60.
cases.script:
out=$(cal -j 2 2024)
mapfile -t lines <<< "$out"
[[ ${lines[2]:16:3} == ' 32' ]]
[[ ${lines[6]:16:3} == ' 60' ]]
printf 'Julian leap-year ordinals verified\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented four rows of three months, every month title, and February 29 in the February column for 2024.
cases.script:
out=$(cal -y 2024)
mapfile -t lines <<< "$out"
[[ ${#lines[@]} == 36 ]]
[[ ${lines[1]} == *January* && ${lines[1]} == *February* && ${lines[1]} == *March* ]]
[[ ${lines[10]} == *April* && ${lines[10]} == *May* && ${lines[10]} == *June* ]]
[[ ${lines[19]} == *July* && ${lines[19]} == *August* && ${lines[19]} == *September* ]]
[[ ${lines[28]} == *October* && ${lines[28]} == *November* && ${lines[28]} == *December* ]]
[[ ${lines[7]:34:2} == '29' ]]
printf '2024 year layout verified\n'

cases.purpose: Check -3 around January 2024 includes December 2023, January 2024, and February 2024.
Check -B 2 and -A 2 around January 2024 include the five documented consecutive months from November 2023 through March 2024.
Check the documented British 1752 cutover: September 1 and 2 precede September 14 in the expected Tuesday-through-Saturday cells, with September 3 absent from the first displayed week.
cases.script:
out=$(cal 9 1752)
mapfile -t lines <<< "$out"
[[ ${lines[2]:6:2} == ' 1' ]]
[[ ${lines[2]:9:2} == ' 2' ]]
[[ ${lines[2]:12:2} == '14' ]]
[[ ${lines[2]} != *' 3'* ]]
printf 'September 1752 reform grid verified\n'

cases.purpose: Check rejection of a month outside the documented 1 through 12 range; Bash loadable usage errors return EX_USAGE (2).
Confirm Bash identifies cal as a builtin and the builtin has help metadata, without treating help text as GNU parity.
cases.script: [[ $(type -t cal) == builtin ]]; help cal > metadata.out; printf 'cal builtin and help metadata available\n'
cases.stdout: cal builtin and help metadata available

cases.purpose: Compare all bytes of three documented 22-column eight-line month grids. Days/weekday positions are independently calculated by Python calendar: 1900 and 2100 are common years, 2000 is leap.
